questions.q: In the lab scenario, what did the CMDB Health Dashboard show that pointed to a duplicate-rate problem specifically?
options: A 40% duplicate rate on cmdb_ci_server, while Completeness and Correctness both looked reasonable
A low Completeness score with no duplicate rate issue at all
An error preventing the dashboard from loading any scores
A 40% duplicate rate spread evenly across every CI class
questions.explain: Isolating which dimension is actually bad is what let the investigation focus on identification logic rather than, say, missing fields.

questions.q: What did reviewing the Identification Rule reveal was the root cause?
options: The rule matched server CIs on Host Name alone, which broke when VMs were renamed during promotion
The rule had no configuration at all and matched nothing
Discovery was not running against any server CIs
The rule matched correctly but Reconciliation was misconfigured instead
questions.explain: A VM renamed from TEMP-BUILD-04 to WEB-PROD-17 was invisible to a hostname-only match, so Discovery created a second CI instead of recognizing the existing one.

questions.q: What specific fix was made to the Identification Rule?
options: Adding the hardware serial number or VM instance UUID as the independent identifier, since it survives a hostname rename
Removing Host Name from the rule entirely with nothing to replace it
Switching the CI class from server to network device
Disabling Discovery for all renamed VMs permanently
questions.explain: A serial number or instance UUID stays constant through a rename, unlike Host Name, which is exactly the weakness that caused the duplicates.

questions.q: Why were the existing duplicate pairs merged instead of one record simply being deleted?
options: Merging consolidates Incident history, Change records, and relationships onto the surviving CI instead of silently orphaning them
Deleting is actually the ServiceNow-recommended approach in every case
Merging and deleting are functionally identical operations
The duplicate records had no Incident or Change history to worry about
questions.explain: This follows directly from Lesson 20 -- deleting a duplicate orphans its history, while merging preserves it on the one surviving record.

questions.q: Why was fixing the Identification Rule done before running duplicate detection on the backlog?
options: Cleaning up existing duplicates first, without fixing the cause, would just let new duplicates reappear on the next Discovery run
The order actually doesn't matter and could be reversed with the same result
Duplicate detection cannot run until an Identification Rule is broken
Fixing the rule automatically merges all existing duplicates on its own
questions.explain: Lesson 20 was explicit that cleanup without addressing the root cause just gets undone -- diagnosis and prevention have to come before cleanup.
